implementation_notes: .NET projects accumulate lava flow through package generations: Newtonsoft.Json alongside System.Text.Json, `IHttpClientFactory` in new code and `HttpClient` constructed directly in old code, `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` and `log4net`, ASP.NET MVC controllers alongside minimal APIs. These are all incremental migrations that are individually correct and collectively incoherent. The practical detection is `dotnet list package` grouped by capability plus a scan for the legacy usage patterns; the practical enforcement is an analyzer that fails the build on the old API, which is what turns a migration into something that completes rather than something that is announced.
idiom_name: Newtonsoft.Json and System.Text.Json in one assembly
code_sketch:
# two JSON stacks, both referenced, in the same solution
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
<PackageReference Include="System.Text.Json" Version="8.0.0" />
// enforcement: analyzer error on JsonConvert.* makes it finish
pitfalls: Both serialisers produce subtly different behaviour for the same model (naming policies, dates, null handling), so the coexistence is also a correctness hazard.
`async void` from an older codebase next to `async Task` in new code is a migration with a real failure mode rather than a style one.
An internal shared library forcing a version of a package on every consuming project can freeze a migration indefinitely.
